exposure: late preterm pre-labor rupture of membranes (PPROM)
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit (ICU) admission rate
cohort: 80 singleton pregnancies complicated by late PPROM at 34-36 weeks of gestation
finding: Early labor induction for late PPROM was associated with shorter maternal antepartum hospital stays but higher neonatal ICU admissions and more frequent antibiotic use compared to expectant management.
mod_finding: This study compared early planned labor induction to expectant management for late preterm prelabor rupture of membranes, finding no difference in mode of delivery but a higher neonatal ICU admission rate in the induction group.
